question.worked_solution:
Approaching from the left, we have $x<1,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=2x-1.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}(2x-1) \\  & =2(1)-1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Approaching from the right, we have $x>1,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=2-{x}^{2}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}(2-{x}^{2}) \\  & =2-{1}^{2} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the left- and right-sided limits are equal to $1,$ we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to 1}f(x)=1.
$$
